title: Holding Several Crestline Tickets at Once
content:
**Customer terms — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** A customer may hold any number of tickets at the same time, on any mix of fare brands, because each ticket covers exactly one passenger on one journey.

- There is no cap on the number of open tickets a customer may hold.
- Tickets may be on different fare brands at the same time, for example one Crestline Basic Economy ticket and two Crestline Main Cabin tickets.
- Protection against duplicate bookings is governed separately, by the duplicate-booking rule; the absence of a cap does not permit two reservations that the duplicate-booking rule forbids.

| Question | Answer under this rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a maximum number of open tickets per customer? | No; there is no cap. |
| Must the tickets be on one fare brand? | No; any mix of fare brands is permitted. |
| What does one ticket cover? | Exactly one passenger on one journey. |
